Legs.Subject: FixedPosition.TryCreate — the per-axis arithmetic-shift quotient, masked residue, half-cell carry compare and the unchecked (localRaw − (carry << 36)) subtraction, FixedPosition.cs:265-284
Legs.Against: Oracles.CellSplit — one Oracles.FloorQuotient of (localRaw + 2³⁵) over 2³⁶ and one exact multiply-subtract in BigInteger, with no mask, no shift and no wrap anywhere. EXACT on both sides: the rounding substrate does not arise in this type at all, so the statement is the canonicalization rule itself. ENVELOPE, reached every run: at localRaw = long.MaxValue the subject's carry << 36 forms 2⁶³ and wraps to long.MinValue; the subtraction stays congruent mod 2⁶⁴ and the true offset is in band, and the oracle judges that without reproducing it

Legs.Subject: TryCreate's refusal predicate
Legs.Against: the exact BigInteger test 'cell + carry leaves [long.MinValue, long.MaxValue]' on ANY of the three axes, inline in Subjects.PositionCanonicalExact — and a refused call must leave FixedPosition.Zero, the WHOLE position, rather than the axes that did fit

Legs.Subject: the canonical band is a fact the law states rather than the type asserts: every accepted position's three Local raws lie in [−2³⁵, 2³⁵) — half-open, carrying UP at exactly half a cell — and the declared cell size is read as an OBSERVABLE fact, an offset of exactly half a cell carrying into the next cell while minus half a cell and one raw below half a cell do not, which is what CellSizeLog2 == 20 and FixedQ4816.FractionBitCount == 16 together mean

Normalize() returns a BIT-IDENTICAL value at every accepted position, which is the invariant claim its 'idempotent and O(1)' remark makes; taken with the band statement above this is a real claim about construction and not a tautology about the identity function

the two construction shorthands agree with the general one: FromLocal(v) equals TryCreate(0, 0, 0, v) and never refuses, and p.WithLocal(v) equals TryCreate(p.CellX, p.CellY, p.CellZ, v) — the replacement offset is relative to the CURRENT cell, so a shorthand that re-anchored to the origin would fail here, and where TryCreate refuses the replacement WithLocal must throw

Deconstruct hands back (CellX, CellY, CellZ, Local) in the declared order, so a transposed out-parameter fails here rather than surviving inside a symmetric claim. It carries no CoverRef: MemberSurface excludes Deconstruct from the ratchet

the throwing constructor and TryCreate agree everywhere: the constructor reproduces TryCreate's value where it succeeds and throws OverflowException where it refuses, checked on every swept operand rather than inferred from the one-line body
Zero is default(FixedPosition), is canonical, and is the value a refused TryCreate leaves behind — one object read three ways
FixedPosition.TryDelta — BOTH code paths: the narrow long path gated on a non-overflowing cell subtraction AND |cellDelta| ≤ 2²⁶ (FixedPosition.cs:307-319) and the Int128 path beyond it
Legs.Against: Oracles.CellDelta — the single exact BigInteger expression (cell − originCell)·2³⁶ + (localRaw − originLocalRaw), one branch and no gate. EXACT on both sides; the oracle knows nothing of the conservative 2²⁶ gate and therefore judges the two paths equally

Legs.Subject: TryDelta's refusal predicate
Legs.Against: the exact BigInteger test 'the displacement leaves [long.MinValue, long.MaxValue]' on ANY axis, inline in Subjects.PositionDeltaExact. ENVELOPE: the narrow path can never refuse — its gate makes the result provably representable, and 2²⁷ would still have fitted — so this leg reads the wide path's range test alone, and the reached-paths leg is what proves the wide path actually runs

Legs.Subject: a refused TryDelta leaves FixedVector3.Zero, and Delta then throws OverflowException while op_Subtraction is Delta — one member read through two names, checked by value on every swept pair rather than assumed from the one-line body

BOTH delta paths are REACHED, not merely believed reachable, and both are COUNTED so a gate moved to a constant would leave one arm dark: a hand-listed witness ladder puts cell differences inside the 2²⁶ gate, exactly at it, one past it, past what the carrier can hold, and at the pair whose cell subtraction overflows outright — each judged by the same one exact expression

antisymmetry, stated exactly rather than approximately: where both directions are representable, a.Delta(b) is the componentwise two's-complement negation of b.Delta(a) — which at raw long.MinValue means EQUAL rather than opposite, and the law says so instead of excluding the point

FixedPosition.TryTranslate — the per-axis long add with the branchless exclusive-or overflow test then the long canonicalizer, and the Int128 fallback that recomputes ALL THREE components wide when any one add overflows (FixedPosition.cs:118-144)
Legs.Against: Oracles.CellSplit of the EXACT BigInteger sum (localRaw + delta) against the existing cell, per axis — one derivation covering both of the subject's paths, exact on both sides

Legs.Subject: TryTranslate's refusal predicate
Legs.Against: the exact BigInteger test 'cell + carry leaves the signed 64-bit range' on any axis, inline in Subjects.PositionTranslateExact; a refused translate must leave FixedPosition.Zero and op_Addition must throw OverflowException

Legs.Subject: the branch is chosen by the WORST axis: one overflowing component moves the other two onto the Int128 canonicalizer, so the two normalizers are required to agree on components that did NOT need the wide path — which is the only place their two spellings of the carry can be compared at all

BOTH translate paths are REACHED and counted: a canonical offset one raw below half a cell against a long.MaxValue displacement overflows the narrow add while the small edges do not, and the witness ladder carries both arms

translating by the zero vector is a BIT-IDENTICAL fixed point at every accepted position — the canonicalizer must not move an already-canonical offset, which is the claim FixedPosition.Normalize's O(1) body depends on

the torsor law, exact: where p + d is defined, (p + d) − p is d BIT-FOR-BIT. This is the statement that makes FixedPosition a hierarchical coordinate rather than a lossy one, and it holds because both operations are exact integer arithmetic — no rounding is being tolerated here
p − p is exactly the zero vector at every swept position, cell extremes included

FromLocal(v) − Zero is exactly v at EVERY sampled offset, in band or not: the re-anchoring moves the STORED offset and never the displacement, which is where the cell/offset split shows itself to be a representation choice rather than a quantization
the composition of two translations
Legs.Against: Oracles.CellSplit of the single exact BigInteger sum localRaw + d₁ + d₂ against the base cell, per axis — so the sequential route is judged against the exact answer rather than against the composite route. Taken with the equality below, this states exactly where the two routes coincide: bit-for-bit whenever the carrier's own vector add did not wrap, and by that wrap where it did

Legs.Subject: associativity of displacement, stated with the carrier's wrap INCLUDED rather than excluded: (p + d₁) + d₂ equals p + (d₁ + d₂) bit-for-bit wherever the componentwise sum d₁ + d₂ did not leave the carrier, checked against the exact BigInteger sum on every axis
Zero is a two-sided neutral: Zero + the zero vector is Zero, and p − Zero is the same displacement p measures against a freshly constructed origin

FixedPosition.ToRenderRelative over the eight-row render ladder — the origin, both unit signs, a whole cell, the far-from-origin pair, a cell-boundary crossing, the 2⁻¹⁶ half unit and the reversed far pair
Legs.Against: Subjects.PositionRenderLadder, a constant table of exactly representable binary32 literals compared with EXACT equality and no tolerance
Legs.Citation: hand-derived from the displacement each row denotes in world units; every expected value is an integral or half-integral number of units below 2²⁴, hence exactly representable in binary32, so the comparison needs no tolerance, the claim body forms no double, and the table shares no code and no substrate with the subject

Legs.Subject: THE THESIS OF THE TYPE, measured: a camera one unit from a position a trillion cells from the world origin renders the IDENTICAL float triple as the same displacement at the origin, bit-for-bit — which is the precision claim the cell/offset split exists to make and which a flat 64-bit coordinate cannot make
ToRenderRelative throws OverflowException exactly where Delta does, at the hand-listed unrepresentable pair, so the presentation seam does not silently saturate a displacement the exact path refuses

Legs.Citation: the published-constant leg above, which reads the FLOATS themselves against a hand-derived table and so pins the conversion independently of the delegation; and position.delta-vs-oracle, which pins Delta against Oracles.CellDelta

Legs.Subject: the three axes are not interchangeable: each ladder row carries a DIFFERENT value on X, Y and Z, so a transposed component fails on placement before any value is compared
FixedPosition.ToString at negative and positive cell indices and at the origin
Legs.Against: hand-assembled constant strings: negative cells pin the invariant '-' sign and the 2^-16 local raw pins the exact dyadic expansion, both authored from the text contract rather than captured from the subject

Legs.Subject: the rendering is culture-free by construction: the hand-written PrintMembers names CultureInfo.InvariantCulture for the three long cell indices — closing the one ambient-culture read the synthesized formatter carried, which contradicted the library README's no-current-culture promise — and hands Local to FixedVector3's own bounded invariant formatter. ENVELOPE: InvariantGlobalization is on for this suite, so a hostile ambient-culture control cannot be constructed in-process; the statement is pinned by exact expected strings whose '-' and '.' could not survive a culture-honouring formatter under a culture that spells either differently
